claim: DKS collapsed FL's Spanish European holding company (Foot Locker Europe Holdings SLU, Barcelona) into Foot Locker Dutch Holdings B.V. by an intra-EU cross-border merger. Draft terms were signed 2026-03-20 and the Spanish entity's dissolution by merger was registered 2026-08-28. INFERENCE: a single Dutch holding stack makes a later carve-out, sale or licence transfer simpler, but the step is equally consistent with routine post-deal tax and entity clean-up. The filings mention no sale.
data_point: The Spanish European holdco (CIF B85826006) was eliminated, so the European holding chain now sits in a Dutch B.V. Neither entity has employees. Dates: draft terms 2026-03-20; deposited at the Barcelona registry 2026-04-15; sole-shareholder approval 2026-05-18; Dutch GM approval (unanimous) 2026-06-16; notice signed 2026-06-18 by Larisa Love Chaleff; BORME-A 2026-09-07 #405010 'Disolucion. Fusion (28.08.26)'.
source_name: BORME-C-2026-3816; BORME-A-2026-172-08 entry 405010 (Spanish Commercial Registry Gazette)
original_quote: decidieron aprobar la fusión transfronteriza intracomunitaria por absorción ... proyecto común de fusión suscrito en fecha 20 de marzo de 2026 ... ninguna de dichas sociedades tiene trabajadores
english_translation: [They] decided to approve the intra-EU cross-border merger by absorption ... on the common draft terms signed 20 March 2026 ... neither company has employees.
verifier_note: Verified on boe.es: the BORME-C notice gives the parties, dates, cross-border wording, no-employee statement and signatory. BORME-A 2026-172-08 (07-Sep-2026) shows entry 405010 'Disolucion. Fusion (28.08.26)'. The Dutch KvK number was not checked. Not found in the baseline or primers. The sale angle is inference only; a holdco with no employees being merged is weak evidence of a sale by itself.

claim: FL EMEA's statutory chair changed twice in about 11 months. Petersson was replaced by Gozde Sen Lonell (Aug-2025), who was then replaced by Reid Joshua Sigal (Jul/Aug-2026). Sigal, a DICK'S veteran and COO of FL EMEA (remit includes real estate), now chairs FL Switzerland and FL Spain and is company secretary of FL UK. INFERENCE: the levers for lease exits or a perimeter sale now sit with a DKS insider. This is also consistent with DKS managing EMEA directly.
data_point: SHAB 2025-08-29 (publ. 1006420286): Petersson out, Sen Lonell in as chair of FL Switzerland LLC. SHAB 2026-07-27 (publ. 1006716977): Sen Lonell out, Sigal in as chair. BORME-A-2026-168-08 #399034 (01-Sep-2026): FL Spain SL, director/chair Sen Lonell revoked and Sigal appointed (registered 25.08.26). Companies House: Sen Lonell ceased as FL UK secretary 2026-06-17; Sigal appointed secretary 2026-07-10. FashionNetwork (2026-06-02): further changes are being implemented in the European management team. Petersson (SVP/GM EMEA 2023-2025) was named Schuh President on 2026-07-27 (Drapers).
source_name: Zefix/SHAB (Foot Locker Switzerland LLC, CHE-112.305.091); BORME-A-2026-168-08 #399034; Companies House 02568406; FashionNetwork FR 2026-06-02; Drapers 2026-07-27
original_quote: Ausgeschiedene Personen und erloschene Unterschriften: Sen Lönell, Gözde, türkische Staatsangehörige, in Wassenaar (NL), Vorsitzende der Geschäftsführung ... Eingetragene Personen neu oder mutierend: Sigal, Reid Joshua, amerikanischer Staatsangehöriger, in Amsterdam (NL), Vorsitzender der Geschäftsführung
english_translation: Persons removed and signatures cancelled: Sen Lonell, Gozde, Turkish national, Wassenaar (NL), chair of management ... Persons newly entered: Sigal, Reid Joshua, US national, Amsterdam (NL), chair of management.
verifier_note: Verified: the Zefix REST JSON gives both SHAB entries verbatim; the BORME-A 01-09-2026 entry 399034 shows Sen Lonell revoked and Sigal appointed (25.08.26); Companies House officers confirm the UK secretary change; the Drapers Petersson/Schuh item and the FashionNetwork quote were confirmed. NOT verified: Sen Lonell's current role as CFO of Douglas Benelux (LinkedIn snippet only; search budget exhausted) and Sigal's investor-site bio (page timed out). Brandi's exit was not re-verified. Petersson's Aug-2025 exit pre-dates the close, so it is not a DKS decision. No baseline hit for Sigal or Sen Lonell; Petersson appears in the baseline only as 2023 Investor Day leadership.

claim: Foot Locker U.K. Ltd's CY2024 group accounts (filed 2025-12-01, signed 2025-11-24) show total UK square footage down 8.6% and a limited-risk P&L: 4.2% gross margin, with risks borne by FL Europe B.V. under a Distribution and Service Agreement. The only post-balance-sheet event disclosed is the DKS change of control, with no held-for-sale or restructuring language. The UK board was reshuffled in 2026 (Barnes on; Boylan on and off within 12 weeks; Carter on; Sigal replaced Sen Lonell as secretary).
data_point: Turnover GBP174,991k (2023: GBP163,435k); gross profit GBP7,329k (4.2%); PBT GBP4,661k. SECR total sq ft 285,762 vs 312,640 (-26,878, -8.6%) for FY ended 1-Feb-2025; the table also changed emissions methodology. Officers: Barnes director from 2026-03-13; Boylan 2026-03-13 to 2026-06-04; Carter from 2026-06-19; Sigal secretary from 2026-07-10. PSC changed to DICK'S on 2025-09-08 (filed 2025-10-02). The next accounts (CY2025) should be filed around Oct-2026.
source_name: Companies House, Foot Locker U.K. Limited (02568406): AA filed 2025-12-01; officer filings 2026-04-01 to 2026-08-07
original_quote: Turnover for the year was £174,991k (2023: £163,435k) resulting in a profit before taxation of £4,661k ... These risks are borne by Foot Locker Europe B.V. (under a Distribution and Service Agreement) ... Total Square Footage 285,762 / 312,640 ... DICK's Sporting Goods, Inc., which became the Company's ultimate parent as of 8 September 2025.
verifier_note: Verified by downloading the image-only accounts PDF (35 pp) and reading pages 3, 5, 7 and 33. Correction: 285,762 is 'Total Square Footage' in the SECR energy table, not necessarily selling space. All officer dates were confirmed on the Companies House officers and filing-history pages. The exact next-accounts due date was not displayed. No Companies House data appears in the baseline.

claim: VERIFIER-FOUND (same UK accounts): the FL UK strategic report signed 24-Nov-2025, after the DKS close, states that the UK entity opened 2 and closed 3 stores in 2025 (one closure was a relocation), modified 12 stores, and for 2026 planned 1 opening with 3 closures already approved. This is a hard, management-approved UK closure plan for 2026, likely including Brixton.
data_point: FL UK 2025: +2 opened, -3 closed (1 relocation), 12 modifications. 2026 plan (as of 2025-11-24): 1 opening, 3 closures approved, against a UK fleet of ~59 stores (Drapers, Dec-2025). Net roughly -2 stores (~-3%), which is a modest pace and broadly in line with the ~4%/yr Europe run-rate.
source_name: Companies House, Foot Locker U.K. Limited annual report CY2024 (filed 2025-12-01), Strategic report 'Outlook and future developments', p.3
original_quote: The entity has opened 2 stores and closed 3 stores in 2025, one of which for relocation, with 12 stores modification. For 2026 1 new opening is planned and 3 closures approved.
verifier_note: Not in the scraper's findings; found by the verifier on page 5 of the PDF (strategic report p.3), signed by E J Amperse and G S Lonell on 24 November 2025. It was signed after the DKS close, so it reflects the DKS-era UK plan. The plan's scale is small (3 closures approved), so it does not point to faster-than-run-rate UK exits as of Nov-2025. Not in the baseline.

claim: Named UK closure: the large Foot Locker store at 442 Brixton Road, London closed 'suddenly and unexpectedly' around early Aug-2026, with 'Unit To Let' signs in the windows. That points to a lease exit, not a refit.
data_point: Foot Locker, 442 Brixton Road, London (in the ex-Shoe Zone unit since 2016) closed by 2026-08-08; the landlord is re-letting the unit. This is consistent with the '3 closures approved' for 2026 in the FL UK accounts.
original_quote: The large Footlocker store on Brixton Road has suddenly and unexpectedly closed down, with large 'Unit To Let' signs now filling their windows.
verifier_note: Page fetched: headline, author, address and quote verified; the publication date shown is 8 Aug 2026 (the scraper said 07). Single local-press source; no second source was found (search budget exhausted). Not in the baseline.

claim: AGAINST (weak): FL reopened in Liverpool ONE on the ground floor of the ex-Topshop unit on Church Street. Landsec confirmed the move on 2025-12-03 and the store opened on 2026-01-23. The landlord says the relocation was 'agreed' earlier and delayed, so the lease decision probably pre-dates DKS.
data_point: New Liverpool flagship opened Fri 2026-01-23 on Church Street, Liverpool ONE. The prior South John St store closed 2024-08-31. Drapers: FL has 620 stores in 20 countries, 59 in the UK. The '646 sq m' figure was not verified.
original_quote: Having agreed to relocate from elsewhere in the scheme, some unforeseen delays will mean that they will finally re-open in early 2026.
verifier_note: Drapers and the Liverpool Echo (datePublished 2026-01-15: 'Foot Locker will open in its new home on Church Street on Friday, January 23') were both verified. Downgraded from B to C because the landlord's wording ('having agreed to relocate ... unforeseen delays') suggests the lease was agreed before the close, so it is weak evidence of DKS-era commitment. Not in the baseline.

claim: AGAINST (APAC, weak): Foot Locker atmos Japan G.K. relocated its atmos pink flagship Harajuku to the neighbouring building, redesigned under a 'PINK HUB' concept, and reopened it on 2026-07-04. This shows continued, modest store investment in atmos Japan.
data_point: atmos pink flagship Harajuku relocated to Jingumae 6-5-6, Shibuya, and reopened 2026-07-04 (release 2026-06-26). The Ikebukuro P'PARCO relocation was NOT verified.
source_name: PR TIMES release by Foot Locker atmos Japan G.K.; Shibuya Keizai Shimbun 2026-07-02
original_quote: 「atmos pink flagship Harajuku」店が、2026年7月4日(土)より同エリア内にて移転・リニューアルオープンいたします。
english_translation: The atmos pink flagship Harajuku store will relocate within the same area and reopen, renewed, on Saturday 4 July 2026.
verifier_note: PR TIMES release (issuer Foot Locker atmos Japan, 2026-06-26) and Shibukei (2026-07-02, 'relocating to the neighbouring building') both verified. The Ikebukuro claim is unverified: neither source mentions it and atmos-tokyo.com returned Access Denied. Downgraded from A to B: a next-door relocation of one women's concept store is a small capex signal and says little about exit intent. Not in the baseline.
